note: Feasibility gate of robot epee fencing (scripts/olympiad/fencing/feasibility.py). 'final' = the world the tasks use (arm limits 1.5 x the Panda's, 2 m/s rail, 45 ms lockout, corps-a-corps only with a trunk in contact), 14 strategies incl. the straight-arm running attack 'fleche'. 'fleche_vs_all' = that attack against every other strategy (3 seeds x both seats) under physical variants: with the Panda's own arm limits it won 66/78 bouts, which is why the arm limits were raised. 'history' = the earlier runs (Panda arm limits; phrase runs with the first 10 strategies and the old corps-a-corps rule). Phrase tables: row vs column = row single touches - column single touches - doubles - no touch (both seats). Bout tables: row vs column = wins - losses (both seats), FIE pool bouts (t.38) with the priority lot at a tie.

history.note: scripts/olympiad/fencing/feasibility.py round robins of scripted strategies with privileged state (the opponent seen with a reaction latency). Phrase tables: row vs column = row single touches - column single touches - doubles - no touch (both seats). Bout tables: row vs column = bout wins - losses (both seats), FIE pool bouts (t.38) with the priority lot at a tie. Phrase runs used the first 10 strategies (before counterbeat/lowstop/retreat and the trunk-only corps-a-corps rule); the bout runs are the final world with all 13 strategies.
